name: io.github.Nero-Engine/uk-subcontractor-right-to-work
title: UK Subcontractor Right to Work Checker
description: Live Companies House check of a subcontractor's company, plus the UK right to work duty

tools.name: check_subcontractor_company
tools.description: UK only. Call this FIRST when a subcontractor gives a company name or number: it looks the company up live on the Companies House register and returns its status (active, dissolved, in liquidation), company type, date of incorporation, registered office, nature of business, active directors, and whether accounts or the confirmation statement are overdue, with a link. It also says which work_arrangement to pass to check_subcontractor_right_to_work_duty. Give company_number (8 characters, for example 01234567 or SC123456) or name. Free.

company_number.description: Companies House number, for example 01234567 or SC123456.

name.description: Company name, if the number is not known. Up to 5 matches are returned.

tools.name: check_subcontractor_right_to_work_duty
tools.description: UK only. Says whether a business must do a right to work check on a subcontractor, gig worker or platform worker under the rule in force from 1 October 2026 (Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act 2025, s48), and what to do. Free. General information, not legal advice.

role.description: Who is asking: a business taking on self-employed people for its jobs, an app or platform matching workers to customers, an employment agency, or a homeowner hiring a tradesperson.

work_arrangement.description: How the worker works: as an individual (sole trader or worker's contract), through their own limited company, or as an independent business with many customers of its own.

start_date.description: Date the contract or arrangement with the worker was agreed (entered into), YYYY-MM-DD. Optional.

contract_holder.description: Who has the contract with the worker: the asking business directly, or one of its subcontractors.

tools.name: how_to_do_a_right_to_work_check
tools.description: UK only. Returns the three accepted ways to check someone's right to work, what records to keep and for how long, and the fines. Free.
